title: Power Grid Optimization
short_description: Learn how utility providers trace power flow, find the cheapest way to route electricity and build a reliable grid at minimum construction cost using graph algorithms.

real_world_context.problem: A utility provider needs to connect cities or facilities with reliable infrastructure while minimizing the total cost of constructing connections. Engineers must trace how power can flow across the grid, find the cheapest route between two substations, and decide which transmission lines to build so that every connected facility is reachable at the lowest possible cost.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Graph algorithms allow utility companies to plan large networks efficiently, reduce construction costs, and keep the power grid reliable as it grows to serve more cities and facilities.

learning_objectives: Represent a power grid as an undirected graph using an adjacency list.
Traverse a network with Breadth-First Search (BFS) to map all reachable facilities.
Traverse a network with Depth-First Search (DFS) to explore connectivity.
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to find the cheapest route between two substations.
Use Kruskal's algorithm to build a minimum-cost spanning grid.
Understand how algorithm choice affects cost and reliability as the grid grows.
prerequisites: Introduction to graphs and adjacency lists
completion_message: You have completed the Power Grid Optimization mission. You have learned how graph traversals, shortest-path algorithms and minimum-spanning-tree algorithms can be used to build reliable and cost-effective power infrastructure.
